sections.title: Basic Concept of Seating Arrangement
sections.content: Seating Arrangement questions require arranging persons according to given clues. These clues are based on position, direction, left-right, between, and extreme ends. The key skill is to draw a simple diagram and place people step by step according to the information provided.

sections.title: Linear Arrangement (All Facing North or South)
sections.content: In a linear row, people sit in a straight line. If all are facing North, their left and right are the same as your left and right. If all are facing South, their left becomes your right and their right becomes your left. Always check the facing direction before placing anyone.

sections.title: Circular Arrangement (All Facing Center)
sections.content: In circular arrangement, people sit around a circle. If all are facing the center, their left is your right and their right is your left. Fix one person at the top to avoid rotation confusion, then place others according to clues.

sections.title: Understanding Direct Clues
sections.content: Statements like A sits second to the right of B mean count two positions to the right of B and place A there. Only one person sits between C and D means there must be exactly one seat between them. Translate each clue clearly into positions.

sections.title: Extreme End Based Questions
sections.content: In linear arrangement, the first and last positions are called extreme ends. If a clue says A does not sit at any extreme end, place A somewhere in the middle positions.

sections.title: 2-3 Step Solution Method
sections.content: Step 1: Draw empty boxes according to the number of persons. Step 2: Place the fixed or strongest clues first such as extreme or definite positions. Step 3: Apply remaining clues and verify all conditions at the end.

sections.title: Understanding Left and Right Clearly
sections.content: Always check who is facing which direction. For North-facing persons, left and right are normal. For South-facing persons, left and right are reversed. In circular center-facing cases, directions are also reversed from your perspective.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Ignoring the facing direction. 2. Miscounting positions. 3. Not verifying all conditions. 4. Assuming without checking all clues.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 seating arrangement focuses on simple linear and circular setups. Carefully observe direction, apply clues step by step, and always verify at the end.

tricks.title: North Facing Rule
tricks.explanation: If everyone faces North, count left and right normally.
tricks.example: If A sits to the right of B, place A on B's right side.

tricks.title: South Facing Rule
tricks.explanation: If everyone faces South, reverse left and right.
tricks.example: If A sits to the right of B and all face South, place A on your left of B.

tricks.title: Fix One Person in Circle
tricks.explanation: In circular arrangement, fix one person at the top to avoid confusion.
tricks.example: Place A at the top, then arrange others relative to A.

tricks.title: One Person Between Trick
tricks.explanation: One person between means exactly one empty seat between two people.

tricks.title: Second to the Right Trick
tricks.explanation: Count two positions to the right carefully.
tricks.example: From B, count two seats to the right and place A there.

tricks.title: Extreme End First
tricks.explanation: Place people at extreme ends first if mentioned.
tricks.example: If C sits at an extreme end, place C in the first or last box.

tricks.title: Draw Simple Boxes
tricks.explanation: Always draw boxes or circles before solving.
tricks.example: For 5 persons, draw 5 boxes in a row.

tricks.title: Check All Conditions
tricks.explanation: After completing arrangement, recheck every clue.
tricks.example: Make sure all left-right and between conditions are satisfied.

tricks.title: Count Carefully
tricks.explanation: Count positions slowly to avoid mistakes.
tricks.example: Do not skip a seat while counting second or third position.

tricks.title: Eliminate Wrong Placement
tricks.explanation: If a placement violates any clue, remove it immediately.
tricks.example: If A cannot sit at extreme end, do not place A there.
